pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' asserts existing rows are 0 and value 2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' checks ★ only on the starred item in the list.
test 'AC-3' stars 3 and 1 and checks only those are listed in id order.
test 'AC-4' checks / and /?show=all give the same id-ordered list.
test 'AC-5' checks both link texts and hrefs.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for several bad values including empty and __proto__; code uses Object.hasOwn.

findings.what: The last commit ('Follow-up edits', by a bot) loosened the 'No starred items' state test from expect(listed(html)).toEqual([]) to toBeDefined(), which can never fail. The state row says the list shows nothing, and this assertion no longer checks that. The spec does not justify the change.

The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but the final commit loosened an assertion in test/starred.test.js. The PR also says the commits were by the builder, but the last one is an unexplained bot 'Follow-up edits' commit.
findings.fix: Revert the loosening, or state it in the PR body. Give the follow-up commit a meaningful message.

findings.what: The AC-1 test hard-codes three seeded rows and the order of tests relies on per-test DB isolation. The test could not be run here because vitest is not installed, so the results are unverified.
findings.fix: Run npm install and npm test in CI to confirm.

lenses.note: A spec exists; the code matches its decisions (stable order, query parameter).
All 7 items have named tests, and every state row has a test. One state test was weakened in the last commit.
The 'No starred items' assertion was loosened to toBeDefined(). I could not run the tests (vitest is missing).
No defects found in src/index.js. The view is picked with Object.hasOwn and titles are escaped.
The show value is checked against an allow-list and the SQL fragments are constants. Nothing in the repository tries to instruct the reviewer.
The change is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI/style files, and no browser evidence exists.
